static_traits.name: Liu Haili
static_traits.medical_history: Never received psychotherapy or counseling; no obvious physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, fairly cooperative, calm tone and able to reflect; low self-evaluation, often using catastrophizing and black-and-white wording; normal speech rate

basic_info.main_problem: I often feel I am the worst at many things, especially after perceived failures. This sense of insufficiency and self-criticism affects my confidence and overall well-being.
basic_info.core_demands: When I noticed these feelings of incompetence affecting my racing career performance and my relationships with family, I decided to seek counseling.
growth_experiences: Caught only a very small fish on one fishing trip. Expectations for performance were high when it happened, and stress was moderate; afterwards it produced intense self-deprecation and feelings of incompetence (e.g. 'I am the worst fisherman'), and this feeling gets activated in any later situation perceived as failure, affecting life and career performance.

Similar feelings of incompetence and self-criticism also appeared after losing a competition in racing in the past; although the family is supportive, they have not yet proactively discussed these feelings with family. Over time, such experiences heightened sensitivity to failure, affecting career performance, self-esteem, and enjoyment of hobbies.

core_beliefs: I am the worst (not good enough, incompetent)

special_situations.event: On the most recent fishing trip, caught only one very small fish
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I have not met my own high expectations or achieved notable results, it equals failure and proves I am the worst
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Tries to relieve negative feelings by rationalizing and focusing on own successes, but with limited effect
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am the worst fisherman / I have completely failed at this

special_situations.event: After losing a car race or making a small mistake
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If my performance is not perfect, it means I am incompetent
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Persistent self-criticism, repeatedly dwelling on mistakes, struggling to focus on improvement
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am too terrible; I am incompetent

special_situations.event: Situations where family interaction and relationships are affected
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I perform poorly at work or in hobbies, I will disappoint family and damage relationships
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids discussing real feelings with family to avoid conflict or being judged
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: It is all because I am no good; relationships worsened because of me

special_situations.event: When considering trying cognitive restructuring or behavioral experiments (fishing again, writing thought records)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot do cognitive restructuring effectively, it proves I really am a failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Hesitating and lowering expectations, but still willing to try
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: What if I cannot do it well? I might still fail

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be seen as capable, recognized and respected (proving oneself in career and family)
core_conflict.fear: Fear of being negated after failure, being labeled 'the worst', and harming important relationships
defense_goal: Avoids failure and being judged through harsh self-criticism and high expectations
Not disclosing inner feelings to family, to reduce exposed vulnerability and conflict

object_relations.self_representation: An incompetent failure, an individual needing to constantly prove themselves
object_relations.object_representation: A harsh judge (competitions, others, or family evaluating worth by results)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor proposes a behavioral experiment (fishing again) or assigns the homework of writing a thought record
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: If these tasks cannot be completed perfectly, it again proves one is a failure (treating exercises as tests of ability and worth)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Use a supportive and normalizing tone, affirm the reasonableness of their worries, invite them to break goals into executable small steps, and emphasize the learning nature of practice rather than success-failure judgment.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When recalling or facing a game loss or a mistake and emotions rise
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Turning negative evaluations and pressure from the outside into attacks on oneself, believing everything is one's own problem
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Tone is gentle and firm; helps them identify the content and sources of self-criticism, encouraging replacing blame with concrete behavioral improvements and compassionate self-talk.

manifestations: Having a supportive family yet not discussing one's own feelings of incompetence and distress with them
After failure, tends to self-criticize and bear emotions alone
outcomes: Reduced sense of interpersonal connection,Relationship tension

manifestations: Struggling to enjoy the process in hobbies (e.g. fishing) due to poor results
Tightly binding individual worth with performance outcomes
outcomes: Reduced satisfaction from interests, impaired self-esteem
Sensitivity to failure increases; emotional distress intensifies

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Sets high expectations for fishing and competitions, regarding 'must have outstanding results' as the standard for measuring self-worth
Tightly binds performance to self-worth, hard to digest and integrate failure experiences

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Excessive self-criticism after failure, hard to focus on improvement
Cautious and skeptical about trying cognitive restructuring and behavioral experiments, worrying about not doing them well

positive_force: Has a supportive family and a foundation of social support
Willing to try behavioral experiments and thought-record homework
Able to identify and acknowledge positive aspects (e.g. acknowledging actually catching a fish, the weather and experience having positive sides)
negative_force: Catastrophizing and black-and-white thinking, overgeneralization and mental filtering
Avoids expressing real feelings in important relationships, worried about being judged

target_behavior.behavior: Intense self-denial and self-criticism after perceived failures
antecedent: Only catching small fish when fishing
Losing a race or making small mistakes
When facing situations that require trying cognitive restructuring or behavioral experiments
target_behavior.core_reason: Highly outcome-dependent self-worth evaluation (high expectations, perfectionism) acts together with cognitive distortions such as catastrophizing, black-and-white, mental filtering, overgeneralization
target_behavior.function: Gaining a sense of 'control' over failure through self-criticism, along with the illusion of preventing future failures, while escaping imperfection and uncertainty
target_behavior.consequence: Professional performance affected, strained relationships with family members, reduced satisfaction from hobbies, worsened anxiety and feelings of incompetence
